answer.explanation: Beacon production (lumen/prod) currently keeps web sessions in Redis. The rationale says this is because sessions must survive a web server restart. The decision is D4, and the current owner is Vikram Rao.

Beacon production keeps web sessions in Redis. The approved architecture decision says sessions are stored in Redis in production and staging because they must survive a web server restart. The governing charter says Neha Iyer approves architecture for Beacon/Lumen production and staging, and the ADR is approved and owned by Neha Iyer.

Beacon staging stores web sessions in Redis under ADR-4 (D4), effective for production and staging. The ownership for ADR-4 was updated to Vikram Rao as of 2026-08-01, and the decision itself is unchanged.

Beacon staging session store is owned by Neha Iyer. The applicable approved decision is D4, which says Beacon/Lumen stores web sessions in Redis in production and staging and is approved and owned by Neha Iyer. The governance charter also authorizes Neha to approve architecture for staging, so this decision is valid for this environment.

On 2026-07-01, the Beacon production session store decision in effect was D4, "Redis session store," which applies to Lumen production and was effective from 2025-04-01. The supporting rationale says Lumen stores web sessions in Redis in production and staging, and that it was approved and owned by Neha Iyer. Therefore the owner on that date was Neha Iyer (neha).

On 2026-07-01, the applicable production decision for Beacon's session store is D4: sessions are stored in Redis in production and staging. The passage says it is approved and owned by Neha Iyer, so she owned that choice.

Harbor staging users currently sign in with passkeys. The approved staging-only replacement took effect on 2026-06-01 to trial phishing-resistant login, replacing the previous staging OIDC sign-in decision. Priya Sharma owns that decision.

Harbor staging users sign in with passkeys now. ADR-6 explicitly replaces the earlier staging sign-in choice for staging only, effective 2026-06-01, and the given date is after that. The choice is owned by Priya Sharma, who is authorized to approve Harbor production and staging architecture decisions.

Harbor production users sign in through company single sign-on (OIDC). The approved decision currently applying to production is D3, effective 2025-02-01, and its rationale says this is because auditors require one central access log. The accountable owner is Priya Sharma.

Harbor production users currently sign in through company single sign-on (OIDC). The approved decision is ADR-3, effective in production since 2025-02-01, and it is owned by Priya Sharma. The governance charter shows Priya is the authorized approver for production architecture decisions.

Harbor production currently uses the nightly batch customer data export because decision D2 applies in production as of 2026-10-15. It replaced the earlier real-time export decision D1 after the production incident described in INC-42 showed real-time export saturated the database and delayed checkout; the nightly batch was adopted to remove that peak load. The accountable owner is Arjun Mehta (arjun).

Harbor production currently exports customer data in a nightly batch because ADR-2 replaced the earlier real-time approach for production only, effective 2025-06-01. The rationale was incident INC-42, where real-time export saturated the production database and delayed checkout. Arjun Mehta owns this production decision and is authorized to approve Harbor production architecture decisions.

Harbor production exports customer data hourly on 2027-03-01. The currently applicable decision is D9, which replaced the earlier nightly batch decision for production because the batch window no longer fit the data volume. D9 is approved and owned by Arjun Mehta.

On 2027-03-01, Harbor production exports customer data hourly. ADR-7 (D9) is effective from 2027-02-01 and applies to production, replacing ADR-2 for production. Arjun Mehta is the authorized approver/owner for Harbor production architecture decisions.

Harbor staging exports customer data in real time today. The applicable decision for staging at 2026-10-15 is D1, and its rationale states that Harbor exports customer data in real time in production and staging because partner dashboards need fresh data. Priya Sharma owns this decision.

Today Harbor staging exports customer data in real time. The approved decision is D1 (ADR-1), effective for both production and staging and owned by Priya Sharma. The governance charter shows Priya is authorized to approve architecture decisions for Harbor production and staging.

Beacon production is governed by Lumen’s production scope, and the current applicable decision for release cadence is D7: daily releases behind feature flags effective 2026-05-01. It was approved and is owned by Kavya Nair. The older weekly-release decision D6 is set aside.

Beacon production currently releases daily behind feature flags, effective 2026-05-01. That replacement is approved by an authorized approver for production, and the charter says Kavya Nair continues to approve release process changes for Lumen production. The older weekly release memo is superseded for production by the later authorized decision.

I couldn’t find any supported decision that states how often Beacon staging releases. The only applicable decision returned for staging is about Redis session storage (D4), and the release-frequency note D10 was set aside, so there is no supported current decision to answer from.

No supported decision about Beacon staging release frequency was found. The only staging release note I found is not from an authorized approver for release process changes, so it does not establish the current policy.

Beacon (Lumen) production keeps web sessions in Memcached on 2027-01-15. This is set by D5, which is effective from 2026-12-01 and explicitly replaces the prior production Redis choice only for production. The decision is approved and owned by Neha Iyer.

Beacon production will keep web sessions in Memcached on 2027-01-15. Decision D5 applies because it is effective from 2026-12-01 for production only, and it replaces the earlier Redis decision for production. The choice is owned by Neha Iyer, who is authorized for Beacon architecture in production.

On 2027-03-01, Harbor staging exports customer data in real time. The applicable staging decision is D1, which says Harbor exports customer data in real time in production and staging because partner dashboards need fresh data. It is approved and owned by Priya Sharma.

On 2027-03-01, Harbor staging exports customer data in real time. The applicable approved decision is ADR-1 (D1), which explicitly covers production and staging and says it is approved and owned by Priya Sharma.

Beacon’s production release cadence is weekly. The applicable approved decision is D6, effective for production on 2026-03-01. Its rationale says Lumen production releases once a week on Tuesday, and it is approved and owned by Vikram Rao.
Beacon production releases once a week on Tuesday. The approved and owned decision is D6, owned by Vikram Rao.
